accepted_gaps.title: Phenotype separation
accepted_gaps.statement: Preference, performance, writing hand, mixed use, and ambidexterity are not interchangeable and lack one universal operational definition.

accepted_gaps.title: Polygenic developmental mechanism
accepted_gaps.statement: Large GWAS findings identify many loci and pathways, but the developmental chain from variant liability to lateralized motor circuitry remains unresolved.

accepted_gaps.title: Rare coding contribution
accepted_gaps.statement: Rare coding variation contributes a small measurable component, but the functional and developmental consequences of implicated variants remain unresolved.

accepted_gaps.title: Brain mediation
accepted_gaps.statement: Structural and functional asymmetries are associated with handedness, but a reliable multiscale mediator has not been established.

accepted_gaps.title: Gene-environment interaction
accepted_gaps.statement: Cultural pressure, training, and task affordances may alter observed handedness, but their interaction with developmental liability is poorly identified.

accepted_gaps.title: Longitudinal directionality
accepted_gaps.statement: Cross-sectional adult datasets cannot establish when brain lateralization, preference, and performance diverge or converge.

accepted_gaps.title: Majority stability
accepted_gaps.statement: An integrated model explaining a persistent right-hand majority together with a substantial minority has not been adequately tested across families and populations.

rejected_or_unverified_candidates.reason: Contradicted by polygenic GWAS, rare-variant estimates, and twin evidence.
Existing imaging evidence is distributed and associative.

rejected_or_unverified_candidates.statement: Culture alone creates the population-level asymmetry.
rejected_or_unverified_candidates.reason: Culture moderates measured prevalence but does not account for the full evidence map.

deterministic_core: Right-hand preference is a population majority; handedness is probabilistic, polygenic, developmentally mediated, and measurement-sensitive.
